## 0. The question, quoted

The lane brief (lead, 2026-11-07): "decide whether some finite-register, local, covariant law on five-mode sites keeps an exact Spin(10) whose centre element -1 acts as fermion parity (S-prime, or a diagonal of site Spin(10) with the lattice spin lift from MT1 and LZ1), whose odd excitations are then spinor class and can move (a band with a node and nonzero leading generator in the physical sector of a D1 state), and whether Theorem SC is evaded and why. Either build it, or prove no such law exists in the stated class, naming the step. Check against PS-6 (frames are local) and NN-a."

The route, in the #10027 note's words (branch `docs/consolidate-gauge-matter-registers`, `docs/SPIN10_MOTT_SITES_...NOTE_2026-10-22.md`, line 135): "3. Spin(10) not generated by site bilinears. If -1 in Spin(10) is to act as (-1)^F, the internal symmetry must be tied to the spacetime spin structure (as in Spin x_Z2 Spin(10)): for example, the cone's two-component slot carries the (-1)^F that the internal centre lacks. That needs the 16 to sit in a supplied spinor-index field, which is #10023's part B and fails the gate there."

The object, in `LW1_5.md` line 149: "**Non-Bogoliubov embedding S′.** Let \(S_+(g)\) be the half-spin representation on \(H_+\), and set \(f(g)=\operatorname{Ad}(S_+(g)\oplus1_{H_-})\). This embeds \(\operatorname{Spin}(10)\) in \(G_{\rm full}\); \(f(-1)=\operatorname{Ad}P\). The operators in \(\operatorname{Hom}(H_-,H_+)\) are 16 copies of the half-spin representation. The faithful one-mode hop excludes this embedding; the full-frame alternative below retains it."

The theorem to test, `LW1_5.md` line 196, Theorem SC (e): "So \(\omega'\circ\alpha^n\) and \(\omega\circ\alpha^n\) differ in centre class exactly on \(T\) at every tick. A spinor-class charge does not move."

The success criterion, `LZ1.md` lines 40-42 and `GA1_5.md` line 57: a D1 state is "stationary, even-translation invariant and invariant under each `Ad c_z`"; `H_phys=closure(π(A^G)Ω)`; a band `(d,F,V)` has a node `K₀` with `V(K₀)=1`; "It **propagates** if some `N_j≠0`".

The target it serves, `TOE_ASSEMBLY.md` line 453, CG1 (e): "the spinor 16 rather than the vector 10 (#10027; the #10126 synthesis lists three escapes: "a site-count change, deconfined spinons outside the finite-site theorem, or a Spin(10) not generated by site bilinears")".

## 0.1 Outcome in one paragraph

**Proof: no law in the law set 𝓛 (the brief's "stated class", made exact in section 3.3) meets the target, and Theorem SC is not evaded.** Laws with an exact local `Spin(10)` whose `-1` acts as fermion parity exist: alternative A and a `U(16)`-rishon witness (Proposition W). Neither live law keeps one, gate by gate (Corollary E.1), because every such embedding is non-Bogoliubov (Lemma E). In such a law every odd site operator is spinor class (Lemma E(b)). The diagonal with the lattice spin lift is the same condition plus link-purity (Lemma D). The target fails at a named step, Theorem N(i): the physical sector of a D1 state contains no spinor-class vector, because each local centre implementer is a local gauge transformation. Two further obstructions hold: with link-pure registers the physical sector has no odd vector at all (Theorem N(ii)); and every band made of spinor-class vectors is flat at its nodes (Theorem N(iii)). Theorem SC holds for every embedding (Theorem SC′). It needs only that `-1` is central, that the local group is exact (PS-6), and that a connected group acts by even frames. Under S′ the fermion itself moves; its centre class stays behind with the link's end number (section 5). Odd physical vectors appear only when some register is not link-pure (Example O), and they are then tensor class. S′ changes the answer in the charged-sector reading: there relative spinor class equals relative parity, so odd string sectors are spinor sectors (Proposition C). Whether they move is `RCS1.md`'s open RCS-P, now posed on an (F)-law. The checks against PS-6 and NN-a pass (section 6.1).

**What the literature settles and what it does not.** The continuum structure `[Spin(3,1)×Spin(10)]/Z_2` is standard (Chang-Soo). On a lattice, a gauge constraint on local fermion parity pins static fermions unless hopping is dressed (Chen-Kapustin, Section IV), and fermions then sit at string ends (Levin-Wen). Gauge-invariant odd composites need a second gauge-charged factor (Nandkishore-Metlitski-Senthil Eq. (1); FMS in Afferrante et al.). No fetched work builds a finite quantum-link register whose transports carry the Spin(10) spinor; the `U(N)` rishon form (Brower-Chandrasekharan-Wiese) supplies one with `N=16` (Proposition W(ii)). The search for "quantum link model spinor representation Spin(N)" returned no such construction; this is a search result, not a proof of absence.

## 3. Setting and definitions

These definitions make the brief's words exact. They are four-tested in section 7. None is adopted.

**3.1 One site** (`LW1_5.md` §1, verbatim conventions). Five CAR modes `c_j`, Majoranas `γ_1,…,γ_10`, `P=(-1)^N=(-i)^5γ_1⋯γ_10`, `M^{ab}=(i/2)γ_aγ_b`. The Fock space is `H=H_+⊕H_-` (`P=±1`), each of dimension 16. The site algebra `𝔄_x=End(H)=M_32(C)` is graded by `Ad P`. Its even part is `End(H_+)⊕End(H_-)`; its odd part is `Hom(H_-,H_+)⊕Hom(H_+,H_-)`. Algebras of distinct sites form the graded tensor product: odd elements at distinct sites anticommute, and an even element at `x` commutes with everything supported off `x`. Links are ordinary tensor factors and commute with matter.

**Spin(10).** As in `LW1_5.md` line 151, read `Spin(10)` as the group `G_s` generated by the `e^{iθM^{ab}}` on `H`. It contains `-1=e^{2πiM^{12}}` and `ω=e^{iπΣ_jM^{2j-1,2j}}`; its centre is `{±1,±ω}` with `ω²=-1` (`LW1_5.md` S′ proof, steps 1-2). Since `e^{iθM^{12}}=cos(θ/2)-sin(θ/2)γ_1γ_2`, the products `γ_aγ_b` (`a≠b`) lie in `G_s`.

**Fact 3.0 (`-1` is a commutator).** With `A=γ_1γ_2`, `B=γ_2γ_3`: `ABA^{-1}B^{-1}=-1`.

*Proof.* `A^{-1}=-γ_1γ_2` and `B^{-1}=-γ_2γ_3`. So `ABA^{-1}B^{-1}=γ_1γ_2γ_2γ_3γ_1γ_2γ_2γ_3=γ_1γ_3γ_1γ_3=-γ_1²γ_3²=-1`. ∎

**3.2 Site embeddings.** *Definition 3.1.* A **site embedding** is a continuous unitary representation `u:G_s→U(H)` with `[u(g),P]=0`. So `u=ρ_+⊕ρ_-` with `ρ_±` representations on `H_±`. Its frame action is `φ(g)=Ad u(g)` on `𝔄_x`. The **bilinear embedding** is `u(g)=g`. **S′** is `u=S_+⊕1_{H_-}`, with `S_+(g)=g|_{H_+}`.

*Remark 3.2 (not used).* Every continuous homomorphism from `G_s` into the even frames `(U(16)×U(16))/U(1)` comes from some `u`: the Lie algebra map lands in the semisimple part and integrates on the simply connected group. Nothing below uses this: every proof uses only `u(-1)`.

**Condition (F)** (the route-3 condition): `Ad u(-1)=Ad P` on `𝔄_x`.

**3.3 The law set.** *Definition 3.3.* A law is in the **law set 𝓛** if it has:
- (L1) PS-5 sites on `Z³` and the quasi-local algebra `𝔄` of `LW1_5.md` §1;
- (L2) on each nearest-neighbour link `ℓ=(x,y)`, a finite-dimensional register `H_ℓ` (PS-6r) with two commuting continuous unitary representations `ρ_{ℓ,x}`, `ρ_{ℓ,y}` of `G_s` (the end actions);
- (L3) one site embedding `u`, the same at every site;
- (L4) local gauge transformations: `Γ_x(g)` acts as `Ad u(g)` on `𝔄_x`, as `Ad ρ_{ℓ,x}(g)` on `H_ℓ` for each link `ℓ∋x`, and as the identity on all other sites and links. It is implemented by the local unitary `Z_x(g)=u_x(g)⊗⊗_{ℓ∋x}ρ_{ℓ,x}(g)`;
- (L5) an update: a local automorphism `α` of `𝔄` in the form of `LW1.md` E1 (a finite-depth product of layers of finite-support even gates), with `α∘Γ_x(g)=Γ_x(g)∘α` for every site `x` and every `g∈G_s`.

*Remark 3.3′ (scope).* (L3) may be relaxed to site-dependent embeddings `u_x`: every proof below treats one site at a time, and (F) is then imposed at each site. (L2) and (L4) take the register change at `x` to be a product of end actions that commute with the other ends, which is Theorem SC's own hypothesis (`LW1_5.md` line 187). Entangled register changes (`TOE_ASSEMBLY.md` section 3.4, B5b-T) are outside 𝓛. Theorem N(i) below holds for them too, because it uses only that `Γ_x(-1)` fixes `𝔄^G`.

The brief's "keeps an exact Spin(10)" is (L5). PS-6 is (L2)+(L4)+(L5). The law's whole frame group may be larger than `u(G_s)`. Cell covariance (PS-1c) is imposed where it is used. Under NN-a (section 6.1), (L5) holds whenever `α` fixes every local gauge generator.

**Lemma 3.4 (the centre implementer is conserved).** Put `z_x=Z_x(-1)`. For every law in 𝓛: `z_x` is a self-adjoint unitary, the `z_x` commute pairwise, and `α(z_x)=z_x`.

*Proof.* `Z_x` is a representation, so `z_x²=Z_x(1)=1`; a unitary involution is self-adjoint. Two sites share at most one link, where they act through commuting end actions; their site factors act on different sites and are even. So `z_x z_y=z_y z_x`. For conservation, fix `g` and put `Y=Z_x(g)^{-1}α(Z_x(g))`. Applying (L5) to `α^{-1}(A)` gives `α(Z_x(g))Aα(Z_x(g))^{-1}=Z_x(g)AZ_x(g)^{-1}` for all `A∈𝔄`. So `Y` commutes with `𝔄`. `Y` is local, because `α` has finite depth. A local element commuting with the full matrix algebra `𝔄_Λ` of a finite region containing it is a scalar. So `α(Z_x(g))=λ(g)Z_x(g)` with `|λ(g)|=1`. Multiplicativity of `α` and `Z_x` makes `λ` a homomorphism into the abelian group `U(1)`. By Fact 3.0, `λ(-1)=λ(A)λ(B)λ(A)^{-1}λ(B)^{-1}=1`. ∎

**3.4 Classes and purity.** *Definition 3.5.* `A∈𝔄` is **spinor class at `x`** if `Ad z_x(A)=-A`, and **tensor class at `x`** if `Ad z_x(A)=A` (`LW1_5.md` inferred definition 7, for a general embedding). *Definition 3.6.* A link `ℓ=(x,y)` is **link-pure** if `ρ_{ℓ,x}(-1)ρ_{ℓ,y}(-1)` is a scalar; that scalar is `±1`. It is **end-pure at `x`** if `ρ_{ℓ,x}(-1)` is a scalar (`LW1_5.md` inferred definition 7).

**3.5 States and bands** (`LZ1.md` §1, with `c_z` replaced by `z_x`). A **D1 state** `ω` of a law in 𝓛 that is covariant under even translations `τ_β` is stationary (`ω∘α=ω`), invariant under each `τ_β`, and invariant under each `Ad z_x`. Write `(H,π,Ω)` for its GNS triple and `Ũ`, `T_β`, `U_x` for the implementers of `α`, `τ_β`, `Ad z_x` that fix `Ω`. Write `𝔄^G` for the elements fixed by every `Γ_x(g)` and `H_phys=closure(π(𝔄^G)Ω)`. When `ω∘θ=ω` for matter parity `θ`, write `U_θ` and `H_even`, `H_odd`. A **band**, **node**, the generators `N_j` and **propagates** are as in `LZ1.md` line 42. *Definition 3.7.* A vector `v∈H` is **spinor class at `x`** if `U_xv=-v`.

**3.6 The target, made exact.** *(T)* There are a law in 𝓛 with (F), a D1 state of it, and a band `(d,F,V)` such that the image of `F` lies in `H_phys`, consists of odd vectors (`⊂H_odd`), lies in the closed span `𝒮` of the vectors that are spinor class at some site, and has a node with some `N_j≠0`.

## 4. Results

### 4.1 Which embeddings put fermion parity at `-1`

**Lemma E.** Let `u=ρ_+⊕ρ_-` be a site embedding, `φ=Ad u`.
- (a) (F) holds if and only if `ρ_+(-1)=ε1` and `ρ_-(-1)=-ε1` for some `ε∈{±1}`. Then `u(-1)=εP`.
- (b) Under (F), `Ad u(-1)` negates every odd element of `𝔄_x` and fixes every even one.
- (c) Under (F), `φ` is not Bogoliubov: no continuous `R:G_s→O(10)` has `φ(g)(γ_c)=Σ_bR(g)_{bc}γ_b` for all `g` and `c`.
- (d) S′ satisfies (F) with `ε=-1`. The bilinear embedding has `u(-1)=-1`, so `Ad u(-1)` is the identity and (F) fails.
- (e) Under `φ`, `Hom(H_-,H_+)≅ρ_+⊗ρ_-^*` and `Hom(H_+,H_-)≅ρ_-⊗ρ_+^*` as representations of `G_s`. For S′ the first is 16 copies of `S_+` (`LW1_5.md` line 149).

*Proof.* (a) `Ad u(-1)=Ad P` holds exactly when `u(-1)P^{-1}` commutes with `M_32(C)`, that is, `u(-1)=λP` for a scalar `λ`. Since `u(-1)²=u(1)=1` and `P²=1`, `λ²=1`. Restrict to `H_±`. The converse is direct.

(b) By (a), `Ad u(-1)(A)=PAP`. Odd elements anticommute with `P`; even ones commute.

(c) This is step 5 of the S′ proof in `LW1_5.md` line 157, with `f(-1)=Ad P` replaced by (F). Suppose such an `R` exists. Then `R(g)_{bc}=32^{-1}tr(γ_bφ(g)(γ_c))`, so `R` is a continuous homomorphism. By (b), `φ(-1)` negates every `γ_c`, so `R(-1)=-I`. The kernel of `dR` is an ideal of `so(10)`, which is simple (rebuilt in `LW1_5.md` line 157). If `dR=0`, then `R` is trivial on the connected group `G_s`, against `R(-1)≠I`. So `dR` is injective. Then `ker R` is discrete and normal in the connected group `G_s`. For `k∈ker R`, the continuous map `g↦gkg^{-1}` into the discrete set `ker R` is constant, so `k` is central: `ker R⊂{±1,±ω}`. It omits `-1`, and it omits `±ω` because `(±ω)²=-1`. So `R` is injective. Its image is a compact subgroup of `SO(10)` (connectedness) whose Lie algebra has dimension 45, so it is open and closed: `R` is onto `SO(10)`. A group isomorphism maps centre onto centre. The centre of `G_s` has order four. The centre of `SO(10)` is `{±I}`: a matrix commuting with every `E_{ab}-E_{ba}` is scalar. Contradiction.

(d) On `H_+`, `S_+(-1)=-1`, since `-1=e^{2πiM^{12}}` and `M^{12}=n_1-1/2` has half-integer eigenvalues; `ρ_-=1`. So `u(-1)=-P`. For the bilinear embedding, `u(-1)=e^{2πiM^{12}}=-1` on all of `H`.

(e) `Ad u(g)(X)=ρ_+(g)Xρ_-(g)^{-1}` on `X∈Hom(H_-,H_+)`. ∎

*Remark E.2 (the carriers are not CAR modes).* Fix orthonormal bases `|α⟩` of `H_+` and `|i⟩` of `H_-`, and put `E_{αi}=|α⟩⟨i|`. Under S′, `E_{·i}` transforms as `S_+` for each `i`. These 256 odd operators are not CAR modes: `E_{αi}E_{βj}=0` and `{E_{αi},E_{βj}^†}=δ_{ij}|α⟩⟨β|+δ_{αβ}|j⟩⟨i|`. So S′ supplies a native spinor index (16 values of `α`, 16 copies `i`), but no quadratic CAR band `h(k)⊗1_16` of the kind #10023 part B assumed.

**Corollary E.1 (the live laws keep no such embedding).** Let `u` satisfy (F). The set `φ(G_s)` is not contained in the frames compatible with an `L5-O` or `L5-U` cube generator, nor with a cube gate outside the exceptional set of `LW1_5.md` line 126. So, gate by gate, neither live law keeps `u`.

*Proof.* `LW1_5.md` M (line 120): a cube generator with faithful one-mode inflow at `x` admits only Bogoliubov compatible frames, and gates outside the exceptional set have the same compatible frames. `LW1_5.md` line 124: both specified hops have faithful one-mode inflow. If every `φ(g)` were compatible, `g↦φ(g)` would be a continuous homomorphism into the Bogoliubov frames, contradicting Lemma E(c). ∎

The whole-tick version (a symmetry of the complete update that no single gate has) is `LW1_5.md`'s open LW1-5-T; this corollary does not decide it.

### 4.2 The diagonal with the lattice spin lift

The brief's second form of route 3 identifies the internal `-1` with the `-1` of the lattice spin lift. `MT1.md` Theorem 5 (line 89) fixes what the latter does to operators: perpendicular face half-turn lifts satisfy `Γ_F(u_1)Γ_F(u_2)=(-1)^NΓ_F(u_2)Γ_F(u_1)`, so their commutator acts on operators as matter parity `θ`.

*Definition 4.1.* A law in 𝓛 has the **diagonal identification** if, for every local `A` and every finite `Λ` containing the matter sites of `A` and both ends of every link in its support, `∏_{x∈Λ}Ad z_x(A)=θ(A)`.

**Lemma D.** (a) A law in 𝓛 has the diagonal identification if and only if (F) holds and every link is link-pure. (b) No continuous homomorphism from `G_s` to a finite group (the cell group or any finite cover of it) is nontrivial. So the diagonal can only be an identification of central elements, which (a) treats.

*Proof.* (a) Necessity. Take `A∈𝔄_x` and `Λ={x}`. The link factors of `z_x` act trivially on matter, so `Ad z_x(A)=Ad u_x(-1)(A)`. On `𝔄_x`, `θ=Ad P_x`. So (F) holds. Next take `A` in the algebra of one link `ℓ=(x,y)` and `Λ={x,y}`. The site factors are even and commute with links, so the product acts as `Ad(ρ_{ℓ,x}(-1)ρ_{ℓ,y}(-1))`, while `θ(A)=A`. An operator whose adjoint action fixes `End(H_ℓ)` is a scalar: link-purity. Sufficiency (as in `MT1.md` Theorem 6). `∏_{x∈Λ}z_x` is the product of the site factors `±P_x`, of `ρ_{ℓ,x}(-1)ρ_{ℓ,y}(-1)` over links with both ends in `Λ`, and of one end factor for each link leaving `Λ`. The interior link factors are scalars. The leaving links are outside the support of `A`. The site factors give `θ` on `A`. (b) The image of the connected group `G_s` under a continuous map to a discrete group is connected, hence a point. ∎

*Comparison.* `MT1.md` Theorem 6 says the diagonal identification already holds on `L5-O[S_+]` and `L5-U`, with `c_z` in place of `z_x`. On `L5-O`, `c_z=ω_z` lifts `-I∈SO(10)`, and the lift of `-1∈Spin(10)` acts on all of `𝔄` trivially (`LW1_5.md` Σ, line 204, with `S_+` registers). So `L5-O` realises the lattice form of `Spin ×_{Z_2} SO(10)` with vector-class fermions. Under (F) with link-purity, the same identity holds with `-1∈Spin(10)` itself: the lattice form of `Spin ×_{Z_2} Spin(10)` (Chang-Soo, abstract of arXiv:hep-th/9411064) with spinor-class fermions.

### 4.3 Laws in 𝓛 with (F) exist

**Proposition W.** (i) The full-frame alternative A of `LW1_5.md` line 161 is in 𝓛 with `u=S′`, and all its links are link-pure. (ii) The **spinor-rishon witness** below is in 𝓛 with `u=S′`, its gates are each gauge invariant (NN-b, hence NN-a), and all its links are link-pure. With the cube structure of `LW1_5.md` §2 and `τ_E=0`, its base tick is covariant under the cell group by the proof of `LW1_5.md` B1-U.

*The spinor-rishon witness.* On `ℓ=(x,y)` put 16 rishon modes `r^{ℓ,x}_β` at the `x`-end and 16 modes `r^{ℓ,y}_α` at the `y`-end, fermionic among themselves and commuting with matter, restricted to total number `m`, `1≤m≤31`. This is the `U(16)` quantum link of Brower-Chandrasekharan-Wiese, Eq. (4.3)-(4.4) of arXiv:hep-th/9704106, with `N=16`. The end action at `x` is the second quantization `Γ(S_+(g))` on the `x`-end modes, so `r^{x†}_β↦Σ_{β'}S_+(g)_{β'β}r^{x†}_{β'}`; likewise at `y`. Put
\[
h_\ell=\sum_{i=1}^{16}\Big(\sum_{\alpha}E_{y,\alpha i}\,r^{\ell,y}_\alpha\Big)\Big(\sum_\beta r^{\ell,x\dagger}_\beta\,E^\dagger_{x,\beta i}\Big)+\mathrm{h.c.}
\]

*Proof.* (i) In alternative A the frame at `x` acts by `π` on the odd basis `O_i` and by `π̄` on the `x` slot of `C^{512}_x⊕C^{512}_y` (`LW1_5.md` line 165). Restricted to S′, `π(g)` is the matrix of `Ad u(g)` on the odd subspace, a unitary representation, so `ρ_{ℓ,x}=π̄⊕1` and `ρ_{ℓ,y}=1⊕π̄` are commuting representations. By Lemma E(b), `π(-1)=-1`. So `ρ_{ℓ,x}(-1)ρ_{ℓ,y}(-1)=(-1⊕1)(1⊕-1)=-1`: link-pure, though no end is pure. The same line gives invariance and covariance.

(ii) Under `Γ_x(g)`, with `S=S_+(g)`: `E^†_{x,βi}↦Σ_{β'}\bar S_{β'β}E^†_{x,β'i}` and `r^{x†}_β↦Σ_{β'}S_{β'β}r^{x†}_{β'}`. So `Σ_βr^{x†}_βE^†_{x,βi}↦Σ_{β',β''}(SS^†)_{β'β''}r^{x†}_{β'}E^†_{x,β''i}`, unchanged. The `y` factor is unchanged in the same way, and other sites do not act. Rishons commute with matter, so `h_ℓ` is the displayed product. It is Hermitian, preserves total rishon number, and is even: it contains two odd matter factors. So every cube generator `H_C=3^{-1/2}Σ_{ℓ⊂C}η_i(x)h_ℓ`, and every gate, commutes with every `Γ_x(g)`. Link-purity: `ρ_{ℓ,x}(-1)=(-1)^{p_{ℓ,x}}` (end rishon-number parity), so the product is `(-1)^m`. Covariance: the proof of `LW1_5.md` B1-U (lines 266-275) transfers step by step, with `c_{x,j}` replaced by `E_{x,αi}` and `τ_E=0` (no electric layer). Its steps are the LW1 A2 sign identity carrying `H_C` to `H_{gC}`, preservation of each tiling, and three facts that hold here. First, `E_{x,αi}↦d_g(gx)E_{gx,αi}` extends to an automorphism of the matter algebra (relabel sites, then apply `Ad P` at the sites with `d_g=-1`). Second, the rishon map is a permutation of the 32 modes that keeps total number. Third, under a reversed image the first summand maps to the adjoint summand: `(E_y r^y r^{x†}E^†_x)^†=E_x r^x r^{y†}E^†_y`. ∎

*Remark W.1.* The witness keeps more than S′: the same computation with any `A∈U(16)` acting on `H_+` and `Γ(A)` on the `x`-end rishons leaves `h_ℓ` unchanged. The index `i` is contracted across the link, so `U(16)` acting on `H_-` at every site at once is a global symmetry that no register change makes local. Section 6.1 records what PS-6 says about this. The S′-centre implementer is `z_x=-P_x∏_{ℓ∋x}(-1)^{p_{ℓ,x}}`, the same form as `L5-U`'s `c_z` (`RCS1.md` line 27).

### 4.4 The target fails in every law of 𝓛

**Theorem N.** Let a law in 𝓛 be covariant under even translations, with `τ_β(z_x)=z_{x+2β}`, and let `ω` be a D1 state of it.
- (i) `U_xv=v` for every site `x` and every `v∈H_phys`. Hence `H_phys⊥𝒮`: no nonzero vector of `H_phys` lies in the closed span of spinor-class vectors.
- (ii) If (F) holds and every link is link-pure, every element of `𝔄^G` is matter-even, `ω∘θ=ω`, and `H_phys⊂H_even`.
- (iii) `H` is the orthogonal sum of the joint eigenspaces `H(κ)` of the `U_x`, over finite-support sign patterns `κ`. The tick preserves each `H(κ)` and `T_β` translates it. With `H_nt` the sum over `κ≠1`, `𝒮⊂H_nt`, and every band with image in `H_nt` is identically `1` on every connected `C¹` neighbourhood of a node. If (F) holds and every link is link-pure, `H_odd⊂H_nt`.

So the target (T) of section 3.6 has no instance in 𝓛. Part (i) alone excludes it. Part (iii) excludes it a second time: a band inside `𝒮` does not propagate.

*Proof.* (i) For `A∈𝔄^G`, `Ad z_x(A)=Γ_x(-1)(A)=A`, so `U_xπ(A)Ω=π(A)Ω`. By continuity `U_x=1` on `H_phys`. If `U_xv=-v` and `w∈H_phys`, then `⟨w,v⟩=⟨U_xw,U_xv⟩=-⟨w,v⟩`, so `⟨w,v⟩=0`.

(ii) *Density.* Let `A∈𝔄^G` and let local `A_n→A`. Average `A_n` over the compact group `∏_{x∈Λ_n}G_s` acting by `∏Γ_x`, with Haar measure, where `Λ_n` holds the matter sites of `A_n` and both ends of its links. The average `E_n(A_n)` is local, fixed by the `Γ_x` with `x∈Λ_n`, and fixed by the others, which do not act on its support. Since `E_n` is a contraction fixing `A`, `‖E_n(A_n)-A‖≤‖A_n-A‖`. So local elements are dense in `𝔄^G`. *Evenness.* By Lemma D(a), `∏_{x∈Λ}Ad z_x(A)=θ(A)` for local `A`. For local `A∈𝔄^G` every factor fixes `A`, so `θ(A)=A`. Density and continuity of `θ` extend this to `𝔄^G`. The same identity and invariance of `ω` under each `Ad z_x` give `ω(θ(A))=ω(A)` on local `A`, hence everywhere. Then `U_θπ(A)Ω=π(A)Ω` for `A∈𝔄^G`.

(iii) This ports `LZ1.md` Theorems 2.1-2.2 (lines 50-64) to 𝓛. For local `A` and finite `Λ` holding its matter sites and both ends of its links, put
\[
A_\varepsilon=2^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{S\subseteq\Lambda}\Big(\prod_{z\in S}\varepsilon_z\Big)\operatorname{Ad}\Big(\prod_{z\in S}z_z\Big)(A).
\]
The `Ad z_z` commute and are involutions, so these are the joint eigencomponents: `Ad z_z(A_ε)=ε_zA_ε` for `z∈Λ`. For `x∉Λ`, `z_x` fixes `A`: its site factor `u_x(-1)` is even at a site without matter of `A`, and a link at `x` in the support of `A` would put `x` in `Λ`. Since `U_zΩ=Ω`, `π(A_ε)Ω` lies in `H(ε)`. Cyclicity gives the orthogonal sum. By Lemma 3.4, `α(z_x)=z_x`, so `ŨU_xŨ^*` and `U_x` implement the same automorphism and both fix `Ω`; they are equal. Translations shift patterns. A spinor-class vector has `κ(x)=-1`, so `𝒮⊂H_nt`. From here the proofs of `LZ1.md` Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 use only these facts: a nonempty finite subset of `Z³` has trivial stabilizer, so `H_nt≅L²(T³;K)` with `T_β=M_β` and `Ũ=1⊗W`; the fibre isometry `f(K)` satisfies `Wf(K)=f(K)V(K)` almost everywhere; the eigenvalues of `V(K)` lie in the countable point spectrum of `W`; a `C¹` function with values in a countable set is constant on connected open sets; Newton's identities give `V=1`. For the last claim: each `Ad z_z` commutes with `θ` (the `z_z` are even), so `A_ε` is odd when `A` is. For odd `A`, `∏_{z∈Λ}Ad z_z(A_ε)=θ(A_ε)=-A_ε` by Lemma D(a), so `∏_zε_z=-1` and `ε≠1`. ∎

**Example O (link-purity cannot be dropped from (ii)).** Take S′. On every link `ℓ=(x,y)` let `H_ℓ=(C|0_x⟩⊕V_x)⊕(C|0_y⟩⊕V_y)`, `V_x≅V_y≅C^{16}` with bases `|β_x⟩`, `|β_y⟩`. Let `ρ_{ℓ,x}` act as `S_+` on `V_x` and trivially elsewhere, and `ρ_{ℓ,y}` as `S_+` on `V_y` and trivially elsewhere. These commute. Put
\[
Y_{\ell,x,i}=\sum_\beta|\beta_x\rangle\langle0_x|\otimes E^\dagger_{x,\beta i}.
\]
Then `Y_{ℓ,x,i}∈𝔄^G`, it is odd, and it is nonzero. The tracial state of the quasi-local (UHF) algebra is invariant under every automorphism, so it is a D1 state for every update in 𝓛 on these registers that commutes with even translations. Its GNS vector `π(Y_{ℓ,x,i})Ω` is nonzero, odd and physical.

*Proof.* Under `Γ_x(g)`, `|β_x⟩⟨0_x|↦Σ_{β'}S_{β'β}|β'_x⟩⟨0_x|` and `E^†_{x,βi}↦Σ_{β'}\bar S_{β'β}E^†_{x,β'i}`; the contraction is unchanged, as in Proposition W(ii). `Γ_y` and the other sites do not act. The factor `E^†` is odd. The trace of a UHF algebra is its unique tracial state, and `τ∘β` is tracial for every automorphism `β`. The trace is faithful, so `‖π(Y)Ω‖²=τ(Y^*Y)>0`. Here `ρ_{ℓ,x}(-1)ρ_{ℓ,y}(-1)` is `+1` on `C|0_x⟩⊕C|0_y⟩` and `-1` on `V_x⊕V_y`: not link-pure. ∎

`Y` has the shape of the gauge-invariant electron `c=fτ^x` of Nandkishore-Metlitski-Senthil (arXiv:1201.5998, Eq. (1)) and of the FMS lepton of Afferrante et al. (arXiv:2011.02301): a gauge-charged fermion times a gauge-charged partner. Here the partner is a link register charged at one end. By (i), `π(Y)Ω` is tensor class at every site: the spinor index is contracted away. So Example O does not give an instance of (T).

**Where the 16 can and cannot be read.** In the field representation, a spinor-class vector lies in `H_nt`, where bands are flat (iii). In `H_phys` there is no spinor-class vector (i). Under (F) with link-purity, `H_phys` has no odd vector at all (ii). What remains is a charged-sector representation of `𝔄^G`. Section 6.2 shows that there (F) changes the class of the odd sector from vector to spinor.

## 5. Theorem SC: not evaded, and why

**Theorem SC′.** Statements (a)-(e) of Theorem SC (`LW1_5.md` lines 187-198) hold for every law in 𝓛 and every site embedding `u`, with `z_x=Z_x(-1)` from Lemma 3.4. In particular, under (F), every odd element of `𝔄_x` is spinor class at `x` (Lemma E(b)). So an undressed odd excitation at `x` flips the centre class at `x`, and by SC′(e) the flip stays at `x` at every tick.

*Proof.* The proof of SC in `LW1_5.md` line 198 uses four facts. (1) `z_x` is a product of commuting self-adjoint unitaries, one site factor and one factor per link end. Lemma 3.4 gives this, with site factor `u_x(-1)` in place of the scalar `-1`. (2) `α(z_x)=z_x`. Lemma 3.4 gives this from (L5) alone, using Fact 3.0. (3) In (b): "For `x∉S` the site factor of `z_x` is a scalar". This is the one step that uses the site factor beyond its being an even self-adjoint unitary. Replace it by: `u_x(-1)` commutes with `P_x`, so it is even, and an even element at `x` commutes with every element supported off `x`. The end factors of `z_x` act on links at `x`, which lie outside the support of `O` when `x∉S`. So `Ad z_x` fixes `O` for `x∉S`. (4) Parts (c)-(e) use only that the `Ad z_x` are commuting involutive automorphisms fixed by `α`, together with Cauchy-Schwarz. ∎

**Why SC is not evaded.** SC′ rests on three facts. None depends on how `Spin(10)` sits in the site algebra.
1. `-1` is a central involution of `Spin(10)`, and a commutator (Fact 3.0).
2. The update commutes with every local gauge transformation: (L5), which is PS-6 with an exact local group.
3. A connected group acts by even frames (`[u(g),P]=0`), so the site factor of `z_x` is even.

Route 3 changes which operators are spinor class: under (F), all odd ones (Lemma E(b)); under the bilinear embedding, none on matter (`LW1_5.md` F and K). It does not touch the conservation law that pins the class. An escape from SC′ has to leave its hypotheses or its object. Examples: drop fact 2 (no exact local `Spin(10)`); read the charge outside the field representation (charged sectors, section 6.2); change the site set (#10038's route 1); use register changes outside (L2) and (L4) (Remark 3.3′). This list is not claimed to be complete. Fact 1 holds for every `Spin(10)`. Fact 3 holds for every continuous site action: the image of the connected group `G_s` lies in the identity component of `G_full`, which is the group of even frames (`LW1_5.md` C, line 108).

**SC′ is the Gauss law; the fermion itself moves.** Take the spinor-rishon witness of Proposition W(ii). Start with site `x` in `H_+` (`P_x=+1`), site `y` in `H_-` (`P_y=-1`), and end rishon numbers `(p_x,p_y)` on `ℓ=(x,y)`. Here `z_x=-P_x(-1)^{p_x}·(\text{other ends})`. The first summand of `h_ℓ` moves the spinor from `x` to `y` (now `P_x=-1`, `P_y=+1`) and one rishon from the `y`-end to the `x`-end (now `p_x+1`, `p_y-1`). Then `-P_x(-1)^{p_x}` goes from `-(-1)^{p_x}` to `-(-1)(-1)^{p_x+1}=-(-1)^{p_x}`: unchanged. Likewise `-P_y(-1)^{p_y}` is unchanged. The odd matter has moved to `y`; the centre class has stayed at `x`, carried by the link's end number. This is the lattice picture of Levin-Wen (arXiv:cond-mat/0302460, abstract: fermions are "the newly created particles appearing at the endpoints of the string") and of the gauged-parity model of Chen-Kapustin (arXiv:1807.07081, Section IV, Eq. (69)), where fermions without dressed hopping are static. The same mechanism explains `LW1_5.md` line 185 ("this construction alone gives no moving excitation") for mixed registers.

**What the S′ change amounts to in SC's terms.** Under the bilinear embedding the centre class of matter is trivial, so SC's spinor-class charges come only from end-mixed link operators (`LW1_5.md` line 202). Under (F) every odd matter operator is one. So route 3 does not make spinor charges mobile; it makes every fermion a spinor charge in SC's sense, and SC′ then pins the charge, not the fermion.

## 6. Checks, and the one place S′ changes the answer

### 6.1 PS-6 and NN-a

**NN-a** (`TOE_ASSEMBLY.md` line 235): "Its automorphism `α` fixes every local gauge generator. ... Gauge invariance and cell covariance are required of the complete update only." Every result of sections 3-5 uses the update only through (L5). (L5) follows from NN-a: if `α` fixes `𝒢^{ab}_x=du(M^{ab})+Σ_{ℓ∋x}dρ_{ℓ,x}(M^{ab})`, it commutes with `Ad e^{iθ𝒢^{ab}_x}=Γ_x(e^{iθM^{ab}})`, and these generate `Γ_x(G_s)`. Lemma 3.4 then gives `α(z_x)=z_x` without asking anything of single gates. So Theorem N and Theorem SC′ hold under NN-a, gauge-variant compilation steps included. Theorem N(i) does not use the update at all beyond the D1 property. The witnesses of Proposition W have gauge-invariant gates (NN-b), so they meet NN-a. NN-a's compilation of cube gates into nearest-neighbour factors (`GA1_5_REFEREE.md` Proposition C) is not re-run for the spinor-rishon witness.

**PS-6** (`TOE_ASSEMBLY.md` line 133): "The internal frame of each site's possibilities is local. Each nearest-neighbour link carries a register that transports frames between its two sites. The update is unchanged when the frame at one site and the registers on its links are changed together."
- The law set 𝓛 is PS-6 with frame group containing `u(G_s)`: (L2) is the register, (L4) the combined change, (L5) "unchanged".
- The no-go uses PS-6's locality and nothing else about it. The local implementer `z_x` exists because the frame at one site can be changed alone. Without locality there is no `z_x`, and Theorem SC′ and Theorem N(i), (iii) have nothing to say.
- Both witnesses keep S′ in PS-6's sense. Alternative A keeps every site frame. The spinor-rishon witness keeps `U(16)` on `H_+` locally (Remark W.1).
- Remark W.1 found a global `U(16)` on `H_-` in the spinor-rishon witness that no register change makes local. One plain reading of PS-6 (PS-6-all, section 7.2, not proposed) makes every internal frame symmetry local. Under it, the witness needs a second rishon set carrying the `H_-` index; the extra local factor changes nothing in Theorems N and SC′, which hold for every law in 𝓛.
- A `Spin(10)` acting on `H_-` at every site at once is not a local frame. It is outside the law set 𝓛. Such a group could act on gauge-invariant composites like `Y` of Example O, but it would be a flavour group, not CG1's: CG1(b) lists PS-6 among its premises and imports GA1, whose gauge group is the local frame group. No claim is made about it here.

**PS-1c (cell covariance)** is used only in Proposition W. Theorem N needs only even-translation covariance with `τ_β(z_x)=z_{x+2β}`.

### 6.2 Charged sectors: S′ makes the odd sector a 16

`TOE_ASSEMBLY.md` section 3.6 names R-CS^str, with `χ_tot` over parity-sharp backgrounds, as the working candidate for odd sectors (not adopted). `RCS1.md` Theorems 1-3 are proved for the two live laws with `c_z`. Their proofs use only: `c_z` is the implementer of a central element of the local group, `α(c_z)=c_z`, the `c_z` commute, and `∏_{z∈Λ}c_z` factors into site factors, interior-link scalars and boundary end factors (`RCS1.md` lines 36-62).

**Proposition C.** Let a law in 𝓛 satisfy (F), with every link link-pure.
- (a) `RCS1.md` Theorems 1-3 hold with `c_z:=z_z`. The Gauss identity reads `∏_{z∈Λ}z_z=ε^{|Λ|}s_ΛP_ΛF_{∂Λ}`, with `s_Λ=∏_{ℓ∈L_{int}(Λ)}ρ_{ℓ,x}(-1)ρ_{ℓ,y}(-1)` (a scalar) and `F_{∂Λ}=∏_{ℓ∈∂Λ}ρ_{ℓ,in(ℓ)}(-1)`. For factor sectors localized in a finite set relative to a factor sector, the relative class `χ` of `RCS1.md` Theorem 3 computed with the `z_z` is the relative parity. So, under (F), *relative spinor class and relative parity are the same label*.
- (b) On `L5-O[S_+]`, the lift of `-1∈Spin(10)` is a scalar at every site (`LW1_5.md` Σ, line 204). So every sector of `L5-O` has relative spinor class `+1`. Its odd sectors are odd in the `ω_z`-label (`χ_tot=-1`) and trivial in the `z`-label: the far end of an `L5-O` string carries the vector index of `γ_{x,a}` (`RCS1.md` line 84), on which `-1∈Spin(10)` acts trivially.
- (c) In the spinor-rishon witness, put `(T_i)_{ab}=r^{ℓ_i,y_{i-1}}_a r^{ℓ_i,y_i†}_b` (the `RCS1.md` line 84 form with 16 flavours) and `ψ^†_{x,a}=E_{x,ai_0}` for a fixed `i_0`. The straight string `B_{r,b}(x)=Σ_aψ^†_{x,a}(T_1⋯T_{2r})_{ab}` is odd, spinor class at the far end `y_{2r}`, and tensor class at every other site.
- (d) `RCS1.md` Theorem 3's conclusion holds: a finitely localized sector of odd relative parity over a cell-periodic background has no implemented nonzero translation. `RCS1.md` Corollary 9 holds verbatim: covariantly chosen ray sectors that are pairwise disjoint across transverse positions and tick-equivalent give only transversely flat bands.

*Proof.* (a) `Z_z(g)z_zZ_z(g)^{-1}=Z_z(g(-1)g^{-1})=z_z`, because `-1` is central in `G_s`. For `x≠z`, `Z_x(g)` commutes with `z_z`: on a shared link the end actions commute, and the site factors are even elements at different sites. So `z_z∈𝔄^G`. Its adjoint action is `Γ_z(-1)`, which fixes `𝔄^G`, so `z_z` is central in `𝔄^G` and a scalar in every factor representation. Lemma 3.4 gives `α(z_z)=z_z`. Multiply the factors: the site factor is `u(-1)=εP` by Lemma E(a); interior links give scalars by link-purity; boundary links give one end factor each. The proof of `RCS1.md` Theorem 3 (line 60) divides two instances of this identity; the scalars cancel, leaving the ratio of `π(P_{Λ'})` and `π₀(P_{Λ'})`, which is the relative parity. (b) `LW1_5.md` line 204: with one scalar end class `ε` on the six ends, `z_x=-ε^6=-1`. On `S_+` every end is pure. A scalar `z_x` gives every factor sector the same value. (c) Each `T_i` is a product of an annihilator at the `y_{i-1}`-end and a creator at the `y_i`-end of `ℓ_i`. At `x`, `E_{x,ai_0}` transforms like a creator of `S_+` and `r^{ℓ_1,x}_a` like an annihilator, so the contraction over `a` is fixed by `Γ_x`, as in Proposition W(ii). At an interior `y_i`, the creator of `ℓ_i` and the annihilator of `ℓ_{i+1}` are contracted, and are fixed for the same reason. At `y_{2r}` the free index sits on one creator at the `y_{2r}`-end of `ℓ_{2r}`, on which `ρ(-1)=-1`. No other factor of `B` is acted on by `z_{y_{2r}}`. So `Ad z_{y_{2r}}(B)=-B`, and `Ad z_y(B)=B` for every other `y`. `B` contains one odd matter factor. (d) `RCS1.md` Theorem 3's proof uses (a) and the cell-periodicity of the background. `RCS1.md` Corollary 9's proof (line 127) uses only `RCS1.md` Lemma 5.1, Theorem 5 and Lemma 6, which are statements about covariant representations, not about the law. ∎

**What Proposition C says.** Under (F) the 16 can be read where odd sectors are read: in charged-sector representations of `𝔄^G`, as the relative spinor class of a `χ_tot`-odd sector. There the class is spinor (for the strings of Proposition C(c), the far end carries `S_+`), where on `L5-O` it is vector. Whether such a sector carries a band with a node and nonzero leading generator is `RCS1.md`'s open RCS-P, posed on an (F)-law; Proposition C(d) constrains any example exactly as Corollary 9 constrains the live laws. This file does not answer RCS-P.

## 7. Four tests

A reading, specification or definition fails if it (1) states or fixes a part's target, (2) is open-ended so a part can add to it, (3) settles a downstream physics question by premise, or (4) adds structure or constants its own reasons do not need. P = pass, C = conditional, F = fail. These are pass-1 judgments.

## 8. Route 3 beside routes 1 and 2

The consolidated note (line 1139) records route 1 as tested in #10038 and route 2 in #10045. This section compares labels; it proves only the two short facts marked.

- **Route 1, site count** (#10038, line 1202): under the bilinear embedding "the centre is z = (-1)^F (-i)^Ns, so a change of site count by dn carries a spinor class iff dn is odd". *Fact 8.1.* Under (F) the site factor of `z_x` is `εP_x` (Lemma E(a)), with no factor attached to the presence of a site. Under S′ (`ε=-1`) a site in `H_+` contributes `-1` and a site in `H_-` contributes `+1`. So route 1's label (site-count parity) and route 3's label (fermion parity) are different functions. This file does not combine the two routes.
- **Route 2, the centre and spinons** (#10045, line 1204): "(A, exact) z_v = -i (-1)^F_v, so z_v^2 = -1 is a c-number, and every matter operator has Z4 charge 0 or 2". *Fact 8.2.* Under S′, `ω` acts on `Hom(H_-,H_+)` by the scalar `S_+(ω)=-i` and on `Hom(H_+,H_-)` by `+i`. *Proof.* `ω=e^{iπΣ_j(n_j-1/2)}=e^{-5iπ/2}P=-iP`, which is `-i` on `H_+`; `Ad(S_+(ω)⊕1)` multiplies `Hom(H_-,H_+)` by `-i`. ∎ So under S′ odd matter carries `Z_4` charge `±1`, and #10045(A) is a statement about the bilinear embedding. #10045's static-background theorem is the `Z_4` analogue of Theorem SC; for the `Z_2={±1}` part, Theorem SC′ gives the same conclusion under (F). Routes 2 and 3 meet in Proposition C: under (F), odd charged sectors are spinor sectors.
- **#10023 part B** (line 827: "part B assumes a supplied 16-component spinor-index field"): S′ supplies the index natively (Remark E.2), but its carriers are not CAR modes, so part B's free band `h(k)⊗1_16` does not come from them. Theorem N shows that supply is not the only obstacle once `Spin(10)` is a local frame (PS-6): a spinor-class odd excitation is then pinned by the Gauss law (Theorem SC′) and absent from `H_phys`. Part B's setting is a free band `h(k)⊗1_16` with no link registers, so it is outside 𝓛.

## FINISH

**Proved here** (pass 1; written out in full above; not yet distilled or refereed).
1. *Fact 3.0, Lemma 3.4.* `-1` is a commutator in `Spin(10)`. Hence any update that commutes with every local gauge transformation fixes each local `-1`-implementer `z_x`. Gate-by-gate invariance is not needed.
2. *Lemma E, Remark E.2.* An even site embedding sends `-1` to fermion parity exactly when one parity block is spinor-pure and the other tensor-pure. Then every odd site operator is spinor class, and the embedding is not Bogoliubov (extending step 5 of `LW1_5.md`'s S′ proof). S′ is such an embedding; the bilinear embedding is not. The S′ carriers `E_{αi}` are not CAR modes.
3. *Corollary E.1.* Gate by gate, outside `LW1_5.md`'s exceptional angles, neither `L5-O` nor `L5-U` keeps any such embedding.
4. *Lemma D.* Identifying the internal `-1` with the `-1` of the lattice spin lift (`MT1.md` Theorem 5) on every local operator is equivalent to (F) with link-pure registers. No continuous homomorphism from `Spin(10)` to a finite group is nontrivial.
5. *Proposition W.* Laws in 𝓛 with (F) exist: alternative A, and a `U(16)`-rishon witness whose gates are each gauge invariant and whose base tick is cell covariant. Both are link-pure.
6. *Theorem N.* In every D1 state of every law in 𝓛: no nonzero physical vector is spinor class; under (F) with link-purity, the physical sector is even; every band in the nontrivial-pattern subspace, which contains every spinor-class vector, is flat at its nodes. **So the brief's target has no instance in 𝓛, the brief's "stated class" made exact. Named step: Theorem N(i), "every vector of `H_phys` is fixed by every local centre implementer", because each implementer is a local gauge transformation.**
7. *Theorem SC′.* Theorem SC holds for every site embedding. It is not evaded. Its proof needs only that `-1` is a central involution, that the local group is exact (PS-6), and that a connected group acts by even frames.
8. *Proposition C.* Under (F) with link-purity, `RCS1.md` Theorems 1-3 and Corollary 9 hold with `z_x` in place of `c_z`. Relative spinor class equals relative parity. Straight strings are spinor class at their far end. On `L5-O` the same label is trivial.
9. *Facts 8.1, 8.2.* Under (F) the site factor of `z_x` is `εP_x`. Under S′, odd matter has `Z_4` centre charge `±1`.

**Counterexamples.**
- *Example O.* An (F)-law whose registers are charged at one end only has nonzero odd vectors in the physical sector of a D1 state (the tracial state). So `RCS1.md` Theorem 4's evenness needs link-purity. And "(F) makes odd physical excitations spinor class" is false: these vectors are tensor class at every site.

**Open by name.**
- **RCS-P** (`RCS1.md` §8, inherited, not attacked here), now also posed on an (F)-law: does a `χ_tot`-odd straight-string sector, which under (F) is a spinor sector, carry a band with a node and nonzero leading generator? Proposition C(d) constrains any example as `RCS1.md` Corollary 9 does.
- **LW1-5-T** (`LW1_5.md`, inherited): whole-tick frame symmetries. It bounds the scope of Corollary E.1.

**What changes downstream.**
- **CG1(e) and R-CG1.** The third escape of the #10126 synthesis, "a Spin(10) not generated by site bilinears", is decided in the vacuum's own representation. Such a law exists, but outside both live laws. In it a 16 is neither a physical vector nor a mobile field excitation (Theorems N, SC′). Under (F), "spinor 16 rather than vector 10" becomes RCS-P on an (F)-law, where (F) makes every odd charged sector a spinor sector. The candidate reading R-16^str (section 7.2) is offered to the owner.
- **Owner, law choice.** Keeping (F) needs a third five-mode law. As law data, (F) fails smuggle tests 1 and 3 (section 7.2) unless a reason other than CG1 selects it.
- **MT1-ii, MT1-S.** No change: under (F), odd species still need a charged-sector prescription.
- **#10027 route 3.** "That needs the 16 to sit in a supplied spinor-index field": S′ supplies the index natively (Remark E.2). The obstacle is the Gauss law (Theorem SC′), not supply.
- **#10045.** Its "Z4 charge 0 or 2" is a property of the bilinear embedding (Fact 8.2).
- **RCS1 R-CS^FMS.** It is empty for link-pure registers (Theorem N(ii)). It is nonempty, with tensor-class elements, for the registers of Example O.
- No law, axiom or working-set entry changes. `docs/MINIMAL_AXIOMS_2026-06-29.md` is unchanged.
